title: CPR & AED Numbers
body:
## High-quality CPR by age (AHA 2020/2025 ECC)

| | Adult (puberty and up) | Child (1 y to puberty) | Infant (under 1 y) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rate | `100–120/min` | `100–120/min` | `100–120/min` |
| Depth | at least `2 in` (`5 cm`), not over `2.4 in` (`6 cm`) | about `2 in` (`5 cm`), or `1/3` chest depth | about `1.5 in` (`4 cm`), or `1/3` chest depth |
| Hands | Two hands, heel on lower half of sternum | One or two hands, lower half of sternum | 1 rescuer: `2 fingers` just below nipple line. 2 rescuers: `2 thumbs` encircling |
| Ratio, 1 rescuer | `30:2` | `30:2` | `30:2` |
| Ratio, 2 rescuers | `30:2` | `15:2` | `15:2` |
| Breaths with advanced airway | `1 every 6 s` (`10/min`) | `1 every 2–3 s` (`20–30/min`) | `1 every 2–3 s` (`20–30/min`) |
| Pulse check | Carotid | Carotid or femoral | Brachial |
| AED pads | Adult pads | Peds pads/attenuator preferred under `8 y` or `25 kg`; adult pads if that is all you have | Manual defibrillator preferred, then attenuated AED, then standard AED |

Full chest recoil every time. Compress on a firm surface. Rotate to the floor or a board if the bed is soft.

## Time limits

| Item | Number |
|---|---|
| Any interruption in compressions | under `10 s` |
| Chest compression fraction | at least `60%`, aim `80%` |
| Compressor swap | every `2 min` (or `5` cycles of `30:2`), during the rhythm check, in under `5 s` |
| Breath delivery | `1 s` each, just enough for visible chest rise |
| Pulse + rhythm check | no more than `10 s` |
| Defibrillation energy (biphasic) | manufacturer's dose, commonly `120–200 J`; monophasic `360 J` |

> **Key:** Push hard, push fast, let it come all the way back up, and stay off the chest as little as possible. Everything else in the algorithm matters less.

## Chain of survival (adult out-of-hospital)

1. Recognition of arrest and activation of the emergency response system
2. Immediate high-quality CPR
3. Rapid defibrillation
4. Advanced resuscitation by EMS and other responders
5. Post-cardiac-arrest care
6. Recovery (rehabilitation, psychological support, survivorship)

In-hospital swaps link 1 for surveillance and prevention. The pediatric chain leads with prevention.

## Foreign body airway obstruction

| Patient | Responsive | Becomes unresponsive |
|---|---|---|
| Adult / child | Ask "are you choking?" Confirm no effective cough. Back slaps and/or abdominal thrusts until relieved. Chest thrusts if pregnant or very obese | Lower to the ground, start CPR, look in the mouth before each set of breaths, remove only a visible object |
| Infant | `5` back slaps (head down, supported on forearm), then `5` chest thrusts. Repeat | Same: start CPR, check the mouth before breaths |

> **Trap:** No blind finger sweeps, ever. You push the object deeper. A partial obstruction with a strong cough gets encouragement and transport, not thrusts.

## Neonatal resuscitation

- Ratio `3:1` — `90` compressions and `30` breaths in `1 minute` (`120` events/min)
- Start compressions only if HR stays under `60/min` after `30 s` of effective positive-pressure ventilation
- Two-thumb encircling technique, depth `1/3` of the chest
- Epinephrine `0.01–0.03 mg/kg` IV/IO if HR stays under `60` despite compressions
- Ventilation is the priority in newborns — most newborn arrests are respiratory

## Post-ROSC targets

| Target | Value |
|---|---|
| SpO2 | `92–98%` (avoid `100%`) |
| PaCO2 / EtCO2 | `35–45 mmHg` |
| SBP | at least `90 mmHg` |
| MAP | at least `65 mmHg` |
| Temperature | targeted management `32–37.5 C`, at least `24 h`; actively prevent fever |
| Other | `12-lead` ECG immediately, treat the H's and T's, glucose control, no routine hyperventilation |

## Special AED situations

- **Water or snow:** drag clear, dry the chest. Pads will not stick to a wet chest.
- **Hairy chest:** press pads hard; if no capture, rip them off and reapply, or shave.
- **Pacemaker or ICD** (hard lump under the skin): place the pad at least `1 in` (`2.5 cm`) to the side of it.
- **Medication patch:** remove with a gloved hand and wipe the skin dry.
- **Pregnancy:** use the AED normally; also displace the uterus to the patient's left during CPR.
- **Metal surface:** safe, but move if there is pooled water.
- **Pad placement:** anterolateral is standard; anteroposterior is an accepted alternative, and is preferred on infants.
